claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA is a single-phase BCC alloy.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA has a density greater than 12 g/cm³.
The baseline alloy has high yield strength.
The baseline alloy has limited room-temperature ductility.
Nb or V substitution for Hf and Zr directly reduces alloy density because Nb and V have lower atomic masses.
Partial substitution of Hf and Zr by Nb or V can reduce density by more than 15%.
The proposed substitution can retain yield strength within 5% of the baseline.
Controlled thermomechanical processing will refine the grain size.
Introducing Nb or V will increase lattice distortion because of atomic-radius differences.
Greater lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion and thereby increases yield strength.
Solution annealing at 1200-1400°C ensures single-phase BCC stability in the modified alloys.
Composition optimization can prevent formation of brittle Laves or sigma phases.
Preventing brittle intermetallic phases will improve room-temperature ductility.
The modified alloy will exhibit elongation to failure greater than 10% at room temperature.
Substitution above the BCC solubility limit will promote precipitation of brittle intermetallic compounds.
Lattice distortion must remain in an optimal range to strengthen the solid solution without inducing amorphization.
The risk of forming brittle phases at lower temperatures is high.

contradictions.description: The predicted success criteria require density reduction of at least 15%, yield strength within 5% of baseline, and elongation above 10%, whereas falsification uses weaker cutoffs of less than 10% density reduction, more than 10% strength loss, and less than 5% elongation. Results in the intervening ranges would satisfy neither the prediction nor the falsification rule.

The hypothesis asserts that an optimized composition can meet the targets, but the rule declares the hypothesis falsified if any alloy above 10% substitution fails. Failure of one non-optimized composition does not contradict the existence of another successful composition.
